intro: Open the industry that matches what you sell. That page shows a UGC ad you can make from one photo. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.
A video can include a script, an AI avatar, a voiceover or captions, and a track from the music library. Send it to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram, or download the file.

faq.q: Why do creator-style ads get watched?
faq.a: Shoppers stay when the clip feels like advice from someone who uses the item. Show the product in the first second, then say the point.

faq.q: What does AI UGC mean for a shop?
faq.a: It means a product clip that looks like a creator made it. An AI avatar says a line you wrote, and you did not book a film crew.

faq.q: Do I have to film before I choose a plan?
faq.a: No. You choose a plan first. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: How long does a UGC ad take?
faq.a: It does not take a shoot day. You review the file in your account after you submit the job.

faq.q: How do I make a UGC ad with an AI avatar?
faq.a: Open the industry that matches the product, put an AI avatar on screen, and use a sentence you would say yourself. Then export the file.

faq.q: Where do the AI avatars come from?
faq.a: They are part of the actor library. Pick a face, and that face can say the line you wrote.

faq.q: Can a listing link become the video ad?
faq.a: Yes. A public product page can supply the photo and the name. Your shop software can still send that link.

faq.q: Do I need a creator's permission to run the ad?
faq.a: No. You can run the download as a paid ad for your own shop. The face was generated here, so there is no creator release to collect.

faq.q: Can I change the video after it is made?
faq.a: Yes. If the product looks right and the sentence is wrong, change the sentence and run the job again.

faq.q: How is a filmed creator unlike an AI avatar?
faq.a: A filmed creator is a person you hired. An AI avatar can take that role when you need another opening for the same product.

faq.q: Can an AI avatar stand in for a human creator?
faq.a: Yes, for the extra openings. If buyers already follow a specific founder, film that founder for the main spot.

faq.q: How many languages can the avatar speak?
faq.a: As many as you can write accurately. Type the line in that language. A cloned voice needs a short sample you are allowed to use.

faq.q: Which language should I write the line in?
faq.a: Use the language already on the listing. Type the line in that language, and the actor speaks it.

faq.q: How quickly can I create a product ad?
faq.a: Paste the listing or the sentence, then review the file in your account. You do not wait on a shoot day.

faq.q: Can the avatar speak in a cloned voice?
faq.a: Yes. Give it a short sample from a speaker you are allowed to use. The avatar can say a new line in that voice.

faq.q: Can I make these ads without hiring a creator?
faq.a: Yes. If you already filmed the product, use that clip and add a generated voice. If you only have a photo, an AI avatar can hold the item and speak.

faq.q: How is an AI UGC ad made?
faq.a: You supply the product photo and the sentence. The spoken line comes from that sentence, and an AI avatar delivers it.

faq.q: What kinds of clips can I make?
faq.a: A recommendation, a how-to, an unboxing, or a review. You start from the photo you already have.

faq.q: What should I look for in a tool for this job?
faq.a: Judge it by whether one photo of your item can become a clip you would actually post.

faq.q: Which industry should I open first?
faq.a: Open the industry of the product you are listing. If you sell more than one kind of item, finish this one, then open the next.

faq.q: How is an industry page different from the template library?
faq.a: These pages group ideas by what you sell. The template library groups them by layout. Open an industry first, then a template.

faq.q: Can I begin with a phone photo?
faq.a: Yes. Use one clear photo with the whole item visible. Daylight and a plain surface make the color and the shape easier to check.

faq.q: Will the file keep my product's color and shape?
faq.a: The file is built from the photo you upload. Start with a picture that already shows the color and the full shape.

faq.q: Can I publish from the industry page?
faq.a: You make the file here, then send it to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram, or download it. You still set the budget in the ad account.

visual.overview: Pick the category. Then make a photo or a video from one photo, with a spoken line, an actor, and captions if you want them.

steps_h2: How to Make an Industry UGC Ad in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: You leave with a file you can post once you pick the industry that matches the item.

steps.d: Find the industry for the item, then add the photo you use on the listing. Say who should care, in one sentence.

steps.t: Let the AI Write the Ad
steps.d: Answer in a sentence you would say to a buyer. That sentence becomes the line in the ad.
The clip comes back with a voice and captions, and an AI avatar in the frame, ready for you to post.

items.d: Show the product in use, then try a second opening while the listing stays up.

Show the product where you sell it, with an AI avatar naming what it is.
Return two openings from a client's photo. The media plan stays with the person who owns the ad account.
Save your face and voice once, so later products can use that recording while you pack orders.
Show the one action that matters, large enough to read, and let the avatar say what it does.

benefits_h2: One Place for the Whole UGC Ad

benefits.t: An Avatar Matched to the Item
benefits.d: Pick an AI avatar who looks right with the product, and let that face say the line.

benefits.t: A Listing Photo Becomes a Clip
benefits.d: The photo on the listing can move into a clip, and you can start without a second design tool.

benefits.t: The Offer in the Buyer's Language
benefits.d: If the buyer reads another language, type the offer in that language so the product stays what you sell.

benefits.t: Set the Feeling of the Line
benefits.d: Note whether the line should feel quiet or bright. The AI avatar's delivery follows that note.
Cut the last second in the editor. The trim stays with the file.
Captions arrive with the clip. Recolor them so the words stay readable on the picture.

more_sections.h2: Everything That Goes Into the Ad
more_sections.lead: You can start from the photo, the link, or the note you already have, and the ad is built in one place.

items.d: A photo of the product, or two sentences about it, can become the still and the clip you publish.

items.t: One Tool for the Whole Ad
items.d: Say what the first frame should show, and the tool asks what is still missing.
If a feed ad moves at a pace that fits your product, describe that pace and use your own photo.
Paste the public product page. Open [URL to video](page:url-to-video) when you want that path, and the photo becomes the clip.
An AI avatar can hold the product and say the line, so you can stay with the orders. Browse faces on [AI actors](page:ai-actors).
Save your own face and voice when the brand is you. Later products can use that recording while you pack.

more_sections.h2: This Tool Next to Hiring a Creator
more_sections.lead: You spend credits instead of a creator's day rate, and a photo you already have is enough to start.

items.d: Upload the photo you took for the listing. That begins the file, whether or not a creator is free.
You watch the file in your account and decide when it is ready to use.
A photo is 24 credits. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. You see the cost first.

items.t: Another Version When You Want It
items.d: Run the product again with a new opening. A fresh set of credits covers that next version.

items.t: The Line Stays as You Typed It
items.d: You type the sentence, and that sentence stays as you typed it.

items.t: Swap the Product, Keep the Scene
items.d: Put the next product in the same kind of scene, and you do not rebuild the ad from zero.

items.t: One Face for the Whole Line
items.d: Keep one AI actor across the products in that industry, so the feed still looks like your shop.
Make a second opening from the same photo and keep the one you would actually run.
You choose the tone, the actor, and the colors. The line does not drift into a claim you did not write.
Ask for a calmer read when the product needs it. You can edit the line before the voice is set.

reviews.h2: How a Shop Uses Its Industry Page
reviews.lead: Each seller opens the row that matches the item, then makes one clip from a photo they already have.

items.d: They open the beauty row and turn one jar photo into a creator-style clip. The file goes on the product page after they check the color.
They open the clothing row and make a clip of the piece being worn. They post that file instead of booking a fitting day.
They open the tech row and have an AI actor point at one feature of the device. The clip replaces a studio afternoon.
They open the food row and make a pour from the jar they already shot. That clip is the one they run in the feed.

closing.h2: If Your Industry Is Not Listed
paras: You can still make the ad. Open the closest industry, add your photo, and the same steps apply.
